`readreq` gives analysts a reproducible way to select, cache, parse and
compare the Australian Government's Resources and Energy Quarterly (REQ).
Use an exact release ID when a result must be reproducible; use `"latest"`
only when an analysis may follow the newest edition supplied by a future
installed package/catalogue update.

## Understand the coverage dates

**REQ itself begins with the September 2011 edition.** The installed catalogue
contains every audited REQ edition from then through June 2026: September and
December 2011, all four quarterly editions in every year from 2012 through
2025, and June 2026. That is 59 editions—14 March, 15 June, 15 September and 15
December editions—not a March-only collection. There is no 2010 or 2000 REQ
edition. Earlier ABARE/ABARES publications are predecessor products with
different source contracts, not missing REQ editions.

Publication coverage is not observation coverage. Historical tables inside
these editions can contain observations from 2000 or earlier, and the first
available period differs by table and series. For example, the quarterly iron
ore export-volume series charted below begins in 1990-Q1. Inspect
`period_start`, `period_end` and source metadata in the returned rows; use
`req_series_catalog()` when exploring an edition's available series.

Asset coverage also varies. Fifty-seven editions have at least one structured
workbook surface. `req-2011-12` and `req-2013-03` instead use a report-backed,
audited Key macroeconomic assumptions fallback. Some early editions use
statistical and commodity workbooks, some later editions expose forecast data
without historical data, and 36 expose forecast, historical and report assets.
Inspect `asset_roles` before choosing a reader; do not assume that every
edition has both forecast and historical workbooks.

## Find releases and source tables

The release catalogue and parser catalogue are installed package data, so
this first step runs locally.

```{r catalogue}
library(readreq)

releases <- list_req_releases(supported_only = TRUE)
stopifnot(nrow(releases) == 59L)

release_summary <- releases[c("release_id", "release_date", "support_status")]
head(release_summary, 3L)
tail(release_summary, 3L)

report_only <- vapply(
  releases$asset_roles,
  function(x) identical(x, "report"),
  logical(1)
)
releases[report_only, c("release_id", "edition", "support_note")]
```

`req_source_catalog()` describes the workbook sheet and table families that
the parser knows how to read.

```{r source-catalogue}
source_catalog <- req_source_catalog()
source_catalog[c("source_dataset", "source_label", "parser_family")][1:6, ]
```

## First local read

The package includes reduced, package-authored synthetic workbooks for
examples. They contain the audited structural patterns needed by the parser
and keep the workflow offline in a clean installation. Official workbook
values and report material remain with their edition-specific sources.

```{r first-read}
forecast_path <- system.file(
  "extdata", "readreq-example-forecast.xlsx", package = "readreq",
  mustWork = TRUE
)

cache_dir <- tempfile("readreq-getting-started-cache-")
dir.create(cache_dir, recursive = TRUE)
forecast <- read_req_forecasts(
  forecast_path,
  view = "reported",
  cache_dir = cache_dir
)

c(
  rows = nrow(forecast),
  columns = ncol(forecast),
  sheets = length(unique(forecast$source_sheet))
)
forecast[
  seq_len(min(6L, nrow(forecast))),
  c("release_id", "source_sheet", "table_id", "period", "period_status", "unit", "value")
]
```

The returned observations follow `req_observation_schema()`. Important
provenance fields include the release, source asset and sheet, content hash,
parser version, normalized period and missing-value reason. A missing source
value stays `NA`, preserving the distinction between missingness and zero.

```{r output-contract}
schema <- req_observation_schema()
stopifnot(all(schema$field %in% names(forecast)))
schema[schema$required, c("field", "type")]
```

## Retrieve and chart a time series

This real workflow puts the complete quarterly iron ore export-volume history
available in the June 2026 workbook on one chart with forecasts from the March
2024, March 2025 and June 2026 REQ editions. The historical line contains 145
observations from 1990-Q1 through 2026-Q1; the three forecast vintages show how
the outlook changed. The first read of each official workbook downloads it to
the persistent package cache; subsequent calls replay that content-addressed
asset.

```{r time-series-data, eval=FALSE}
releases <- list_req_releases(supported_only = TRUE)
vintage_ids <- c("req-2024-03", "req-2025-03", "req-2026-06")
releases[
  releases$release_id %in% vintage_ids,
  c("release_id", "release_date", "asset_roles")
]

sources <- req_source_catalog()
sources[
  sources$table_id %in% c(
    "history_commodity_iron_ore_steel",
    "forecast_quarterly_export_volumes"
  ),
  c("source_dataset", "source_label", "table_id", "parser_family")
]

history <- read_req_history(
  "req-2026-06",
  tables = "history_commodity_iron_ore_steel",
  commodities = "iron_ore_steel",
  concepts = "exports_quantity_iron_ore_b_total_iron_ore",
  geography = "Australia",
  frequency = "quarterly",
  view = "canonical",
  cache_dir = req_cache_dir()
)

history <- history[
  !is.na(history$value), c("period_start", "value")
]
history$value <- history$value / 1000
history$series <- "Historical"

vintage_labels <- setNames(
  c("REQ March 2024", "REQ March 2025", "REQ June 2026"),
  vintage_ids
)
forecasts <- do.call(rbind, lapply(vintage_ids, function(id) {
  x <- read_req_forecasts(
    id,
    sheets = "forecast_quarterly_export_volumes",
    commodities = "iron_ore",
    concepts = "export_volume",
    geography = "Australia",
    view = "canonical",
    cache_dir = req_cache_dir()
  )
  x <- x[
    !is.na(x$value) & x$period_status %in% c("forecast", "projection"),
    c("period_start", "value")
  ]
  x$series <- vintage_labels[[id]]
  x
}))

chart_data <- rbind(history, forecasts)
chart_data <- chart_data[order(chart_data$series, chart_data$period_start), ]
chart_data$series <- factor(
  chart_data$series, levels = c("Historical", unname(vintage_labels))
)
```

```{r time-series-chart, eval=FALSE}
if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {
  ggplot2::ggplot(
    chart_data,
    ggplot2::aes(
      x = period_start, y = value, colour = series, group = series
    )
  ) +
    ggplot2::geom_line() +
    ggplot2::labs(
      title = "Australian iron ore export volumes",
      subtitle = "Quarterly history and REQ forecast vintages",
      x = "Quarter",
      y = "Million tonnes",
      colour = "Series",
      caption = "Sources: DISR REQ; ABS Cat. No. 5368.0"
    ) +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 13)
}
```

```{r include-time-series-chart, echo=FALSE, out.width="100%", fig.alt="Single line chart of Australian quarterly iron ore export volumes: the full 1990-Q1 to 2026-Q1 history and forecast paths from the March 2024, March 2025 and June 2026 REQ editions."}
chart_file <- file.path("..", "man", "figures", "time-series-chart-1.png")
if (!file.exists(chart_file)) {
  chart_file <- file.path("man", "figures", "time-series-chart-1.png")
}
knitr::include_graphics(chart_file)
```

The checked-in figure was generated from this exact public-API workflow so
article and package builds do not require the network. The official workbooks
and extracted rows are not bundled. History is taken from the June 2026
historical workbook and converted from kt to million tonnes; only rows marked
`forecast` or `projection` are retained for each forecast vintage. The table
notes credit the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS), DISR and other named
sources. See the [March 2024](https://www.industry.gov.au/publications/resources-and-energy-quarterly-march-2024),
[March 2025](https://www.industry.gov.au/publications/resources-and-energy-quarterly-march-2025)
and [June 2026](https://www.industry.gov.au/publications/resources-and-energy-quarterly-june-2026)
edition pages for the workbooks and source terms. Use
`req_series_catalog()` for broader interactive exploration.

## Installation, network and rights

Until a CRAN release is accepted, install the package from its GitHub
repository when you have access, or from a local source tree. The installed
release catalogue is available offline; catalogue asset downloads use public
HTTPS endpoints without a data-source credential, token or API key. A
supplied local input or custom transport can use another controlled source.
The default cache is managed by `tools::R_user_dir()`; examples use a
temporary cache so that rendering does not write to a home or project
directory.

**Package code and package-authored synthetic fixtures: MIT, copyright Chartwell
F.** The iron ore figure above is derived from official March 2024, March 2025
and June 2026 forecast tables and the June 2026 historical table; it is not
covered by the package's MIT licence. Each source publication states CC BY 4.0
subject to named exclusions. The tables credit ABS Cat. No. 5368.0, DISR and
other named sources. The chart contains no source logos or Coat of Arms.
Official REQ workbooks and reports are not relicensed by `readreq`; check the
terms attached to the exact edition and use `req_attribution()` before
redistributing derived results. The installed `COPYRIGHTS` file records the
figure's provenance and rights boundary.
